div.head: Hn 20.3
div.ab: Singulorum denique baronum, senatorum — clericorum, laicorum —, ubicunque habeant terram, siue socna regis sit uel non, in capitalibus questionibus socna [regis] est, sicut a (Edmundi), Cnuti uel Edwardi legibus per successiones posteras hereditaria dignitas successit, nisi uel propinquitate uel aliqua dignitate meritorum regis indulgencia quemcumque respexerit, cuius amanda bonitas promouet potius, non euertit libertatem.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 560 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Optimaten, Kleriker oder Laien, stehen in Criminalsachen unter Königsgericht, auch wenn ihr Manor sonst unter privater Jurisdiction steht
Magnates, clerical or lay, are subject to the king's court in criminal matters, even if their manor is otherwise under private jurisdiction
deren Strafe Leben, Glieder oder Wergeld kostet oder in misericordia regis verfällt
whose punishment costs life, limbs or wergild, or falls in misericordia regis
seit der Verfassung des Bekenners, die Verf. auch sonst mit der Cnuts gleich setzt; vgl. Quadr. Arg. 1. 9
since the constitution of the Confessor, which the author elsewhere too equates with Cnut's; cf. Quadr. Arg. 1. 9
lacking in MSS; supplied by Wi Tho.
fehlt Sc Hg [vielleicht vom Verfasser selbst nur nachgetragen; vgl. 88, 12]
lacking in Sc Hg [perhaps only added later by the author himself; cf. 88, 12]
Kn. ohne uel Lond; comiti Hg
Kn. without uel Lond; comiti Hg
et inserted by a corrector Sc

für witan im Sinne der leitenden, angesehensten Gerichtsoberen u. 29, 4 und in Urkk. 9. 10. Jhs., auch Earle Landchar. 70. 283, hier aber wohl auch ‘Reichsratsmitglieder’; s. mein National assembly p. 9{6}

for witan in the sense of the leading, most respected presiding officers of the courts below 29, 4 and in charters of the 9th and 10th cent., also Earle Landchar. 70. 283; but here probably also ‘members of the king's council’; see my National assembly p. 9{6}

Dass alle Kapitalverbrechen (s. d. Gl 4b) dem Könige gehören, wie Frühere (auch Stubbs Lect. 158) diese Stelle verstanden, steht zwar des Verf. Meinung nach einigen anderen Stellen ganz nahe. Hier aber will er so Allgemeines nicht sagen—der Zwischensatz sive s. r. s. u. non wäre sonst sinnlos—, sondern laut des Zitats nur wegen des höchsten Status des Täters die Zuständigkeit dem Königsgericht (s. d. Gl 8b) vorbehalten; s. u. 24, 1 [Stubbs meinte jener Deutung zu Liebe, diese senatores als niedere þegnas von den höheren Magnaten in 20, 2 trennen zu sollen; allein barones ohne Weiteres heisst bei Hn höchste Kronvassallen]

That all capital crimes (see that word in Gl 4b) belong to the king, as earlier scholars (Stubbs Lect. 158 among them) understood this passage, is indeed very close to the author's view as expressed in some other passages. Here, however, he does not mean to say anything so general—the intervening clause sive s. r. s. u. non would otherwise be meaningless—but, according to the citation, only to reserve jurisdiction to the king's court (see that word in Gl 8b) on account of the offender's highest rank; see below 24, 1 [For the sake of that interpretation Stubbs thought he had to separate these senatores, as lesser þegnas, from the higher magnates in 20, 2; but in Hn barones without qualification means the highest tenants-in-chief of the Crown]

Nur durch II Cn 13, 1 über Heimfall des Bocland an den König lag der Gedanke an den Adel des Täters nahe. Von Eadmund I., dessen Name der frühereren Rezension samt Rs fehlt, ist nichts hierauf Bezügliches uns bekannt. Ward der Name nur willkürlich nachgetragen? Vgl. Gl Eadwardi laga 4c—te. ha.{31}—socna est ohne regis{34}—Eadw.—dignitate{38} ‘wie es durch Thronfolge vererbte’—m. d.{40} r. i. quecumque Rs

Only II Cn 13, 1, on the forfeiture of bookland to the king, suggested the idea of the offender's noble rank. Of Eadmund I, whose name is lacking in the earlier recension together with Rs, nothing relevant to this is known to us. Was the name merely added arbitrarily? Cf. Gl Eadwardi laga 4c—te. ha.{31}—socna est without regis{34}—Eadw.—dignitate{38} ‘as it was inherited through succession to the throne’—m. d.{40} r. i. quecumque Rs

div.ab: Of each of the barons, finally, [and] of the elders — clerics [and] laymen —, wherever they have land, whether it be the king's soke or not, in capital cases the soke is [the king's], as the hereditary dignity has descended from the laws of (Edmund), Cnut or Edward through later successions, unless the king's indulgence has regarded someone on account either of kinship or of some worthiness of merits, whose lovable goodness rather advances liberty, not overturns it.
